answer: Approximately 5.6% of the original studies in the Experimental Economics replication project were conducted in the United Kingdom — that is, 1 of 18 original studies (exact proportion 1/18 ≈ 0.0556). The single UK-conducted original study is ee.13, "Deferred compensation in multiperiod labor contracts: an experimental test of Lazear's model" (Huck, Seltzer & Wallace, 2011). Given the small sample (n = 18), this estimate should be interpreted with caution.

payload.hypothesis: Approximately 5.6% of original studies in Experimental Economics (1 of 18, i.e., 1/18 ≈ 0.0556) were conducted in the United Kingdom.
payload.workflow: 1) Loaded meta-regression_study_data_heterogeneity_in_replication_projects.csv (927 rows). 2) Filtered to project=='ee' to define original Experimental Economics studies (18 rows; discipline is 'Economics' for all 18, so project==ee and discipline==Economics are equivalent). 3) Verified no missing experiment_country.o and no duplicate ids in the subset. 4) Counted experiment_country.o=='United Kingdom' (numerator=1) and total ee studies (denominator=18); proportion=1/18≈0.0556 (5.6%). 5) The replication_success CSV has no country column and was used only to confirm the 18-study scope. 6) Produced natural-language conclusion with exact fraction, percentage, and small-sample caveat.
